paragraphs: On Sunday morning, Lily and Tom walked to the pond with Grandpa. The morning was cool, and the sky was clear. They wanted to see the wildlife there. Grandpa carried a small bag with a kit inside. "Why do you take a kit?" asked Tom. "Because I always want to be ready," said Grandpa. "It has bandages and water, and a child can fall on a walk."

The road to the pond had a crossing. They stopped there, because a truck was coming. "Why do we use the crossing?" asked Lily. "Because the drivers can see us there," said Grandpa. The truck stopped, and the driver smiled. A woman with a green bag waited next to them. The three of them crossed the road carefully.

At the pond, there were many birds and some ducks. Tom began to whisper, because the birds were shy. A duck swam to the middle of the pond. Some small fish moved under the green plants. "Let's walk further," said Lily, "because I want to see the frogs." They walked along the bank, and Grandpa washed his hands in the water. His hands were dirty from the path.

Grandpa dried his hands on his shirt. Then Lily saw Grandpa's hand. "Grandpa, where is your ring?" she asked. Grandpa looked at his hand, and his face became serious. "It was here a minute ago," he said. "It is very important, because Grandma gave it to me." "I am her husband, and I have worn it for forty years." The children looked in the water and in the grass. They searched the whole bank, and Tom nearly fell into the pond. "Here it is!" shouted Tom. The ring was in the grass next to a stone.

Grandpa put the ring on his finger and smiled. "Thank you, children," he said. "I will wear it every day, because it makes me happy." At home, Grandma saw their wet shoes. "Why are your shoes wet?" she asked. "Because we found Grandpa's ring," said Lily, "and he is very happy." Grandma smiled and gave them cold juice.
